title: Lewis and Clark with Sacagawea and York, to the Pacific and back, 1804–06
summary: Jefferson sent Lewis and Clark up the Missouri to find a route to the Pacific. They left Camp Dubois in May 1804 with more than forty men, wintered with the Mandan and Hidatsa, where Sacagawea and Charbonneau joined, crossed the Rockies with Shoshone horses and Nez Perce help, reached the Pacific in November 1805 and wintered at Fort Clatsop. They were back at St Louis on 23 September 1806. York, enslaved by Clark, went the whole way.

events.label: Fort Mandan: Sacagawea joins
events.text: They wintered by the Mandan and Hidatsa villages. Toussaint Charbonneau was hired as an interpreter, and his Shoshone wife Sacagawea, then about sixteen, came with him. She gave birth to Jean Baptiste on 11 February 1805, and carried him across the continent.

events.label: Lemhi Pass: Sacagawea's people
events.text: Over the Continental Divide the party found the Lemhi Shoshone, whose chief proved to be her brother Cameahwait. Sacagawea interpreted, and the party bought the horses it needed to cross the Bitterroots.

events.label: Fort Clatsop, and the vote
events.text: In November 1805 the party voted where to winter. Sacagawea and York were both asked their opinion, though neither could vote in the United States.
